candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model (DSM) - 1m
verified_facts: Official 1m DSM covers about 99% of England and includes buildings, vegetation, vehicles and terrain because it uses last/only return surface heights.
The 2022 composite merges Time Stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys and uses newest best-resolution data where surveys repeat.
Resampled inputs use bilinear interpolation and the metadata index identifies the survey used at a location.
semantic_limits: DSM values are not bare-earth terrain and must not enter the primary height-difference extrema.
A 1m grid label does not establish parcel-specific survey identity or accuracy.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model (DSM) - 2m
verified_facts: Official 2m DSM covers about 99% of England and includes above-ground objects as well as terrain.
It combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys and uses bilinear interpolation where resampling occurred.
The metadata index catalogue is required to determine which survey contributed at a location.
semantic_limits: The 2m DSM is not a substitute for the 1m bare-earth DTM.
Object-surface values must remain excluded from primary parcel terrain extrema.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return Digital Surface Model (FZ_DSM) - 2m
verified_facts: Official first-return DSM covers about 99% of England at 2m and includes objects hit by first/only laser returns.
It is derived from National LIDAR Programme surveys captured between November 2016 and May 2022.
Survey overlaps are feathered and metadata index catalogues identify the survey used at a location; individual contributing surveys specify ±15cm RMSE vertical accuracy.
semantic_limits: First-return DSM is an object-inclusive surface model and cannot be used as bare-earth parcel height evidence.
Feathering is a merge process and does not represent raw point accuracy.

candidates.publisher: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
candidates.name: LIDAR Composite DTM 2017 - 25cm (retired)
verified_facts: The Environment Agency marks the 2017 25cm composite DTM as retired and no longer available on the Data Services Platform.
The record says the composite product was replaced by the 1m resolution version while 25cm time-stamped archive data remains available separately.
The historic record describes the retired composite as derived from time-stamped archive data and referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
semantic_limits: The retired 25cm composite must not be selected as a current production source merely because its nominal resolution is finer.
Historic product availability is not evidence that a parcel has current 25cm composite coverage.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Technical Specification
verified_facts: Terrain 50 is the lower-resolution OS DTM intended for landscape visualisation and large-area analysis.
Its grid uses regular 50m post spacing and its contours use 10m intervals.
The product is available in ASCII/GML grid and GML, shapefile, GeoPackage and vector-tile contour formats.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 remains a coarse secondary cross-check and must not replace Environment Agency DTM1m.
Format variety does not create independent measurements.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply
verified_facts: Terrain 50 is supplied online with no registration required.
ASCII/GML/shapefile national supply is tiled into 2,858 10km tiles while GeoPackage/vector-tile formats can be supplied as a national flat file.
OS states annual full-tile resupply each July.
semantic_limits: Distribution cadence is product freshness evidence, not a parcel observation timestamp.
A downloaded tile does not establish EA survey lineage.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data
verified_facts: Terrain 50 ASCII grid height values are calculated from pixel centres.
The grid has 200 pixels per row with 50m by 50m pixels.
GML accompanying the ASCII grid supplies location, grid spacing, vertical reference and spatial reference metadata.
semantic_limits: Pixel-centre values are model/grid semantics, not direct survey observations at arbitrary parcel points.
The GML wrapper does not constitute an independent height source.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 supplies GEMINI-style XML metadata at national and per-tile level.
Per-tile metadata identifies product name, spatial representation and 10km National Grid tile reference.
The metadata structure supports lineage and product identification but is separate from the numeric grid.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 tile metadata cannot identify the Environment Agency composite survey used for a parcel.
Metadata presence alone is not parcel-specific numeric evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 Overview
verified_facts: Terrain 50 is an Open Data lower-resolution DTM for Great Britain.
It provides 50m grid points and 10m contours from the same source data.
The overview distinguishes Terrain 5 mid-resolution use from Terrain 50 large-area landscape use.
semantic_limits: Open availability does not make Terrain 50 the primary parcel-scale source.
Grid and contour products derived from the same source are correlated evidence, not two independent measurements.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 contour data
verified_facts: Terrain 50 contours are supplied in GML 3.2.1 with per-tile metadata.
Spot heights are automatically selected from mass points within closed contours.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
semantic_limits: Rounded spot heights are unsuitable as a replacement for finer-resolution EA DTM parcel extrema.
Contour spot-height selection is derived secondary evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 downloads
verified_facts: OS provides XML schema resources for Terrain contour and gridded products plus viewing-style metadata.
Schema resources support validation and software interoperability.
semantic_limits: Schema validity proves structural conformance only and must not be treated as terrain accuracy or parcel measurement evidence.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 prerequisites
verified_facts: OS states Terrain 50 is supplied as inert data and does not include manipulation software.
GML may need translation depending on the GIS application and software capabilities.
semantic_limits: Software/rendering behaviour is not a source measurement and must not silently change the numeric terrain semantics.
Any format conversion used by the workflow must preserve source CRS, vertical reference and numeric values.

verification_basis: official public internet sources; source authority confidence only
